title: Canonical mate factorization on the explicit affine alternating Cech model
statement: Fix shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], rings A,B, a quasi-compact separated f:X -> Spec A and g:Spec B -> Spec A. Let U:Fin r -> X.Opens be an affine cover, G a quasi-coherent O_X-module, and c a comparison specified by [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]. Put K equal to the explicit model [def-pc-affine-alternating-cech-model]. There exist the ordinary tensor-pullback functor F for g (pinned on objects and maps), a left-derived counit epsilon for [def-pc-derived-pullback], an isomorphism e:Rf_*G[0] -> Qh(K), and an isomorphism t:Qh(F(K)) -> Rf_B,*((p*G)[0]), such that the canonical mate [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] followed by Rf_B,*(c) equals Lg*(e.hom) followed by epsilon at K followed by t.hom. No flatness of G or K is assumed and no invertibility of epsilon is asserted.

proof.text: Use the finite increasing-tuple affine Cech resolution. On each cover member insertion of its index, reordering with sign, and setting repeated indices to zero contract the augmentation. Affine-intersection open pushforwards are f_*-acyclic. The acyclic-resolution argument identifies the sheafified section complex K with Rf_*G. Repeat on the pulled-back cover.

The affine section-pullback pure-tensor formula on every intersection is compatible with restrictions. Tensor commutes with the finite increasing-tuple products. The component isomorphisms therefore commute with the signed differentials and induce the target isomorphism t. This does not require flatness.

Choose the left-derived counit for g compatible with the derived adjunctions. Transpose the canonical mate followed by the ordinary comparison under Lf_B* adjoint Rf_B*. Evaluate on the Cech augmentation; naturality and the triangle identities cancel the units and leave the ordinary affine-section maps. Thus the composite equals Lg*(e) followed by the counit at K and t.

For the specified c, compare its witnessing p-counit with the previous one by right Kan extension uniqueness. Derived tensor of G[0] is nonpositive with H0 = p*G; maps to (p*G)[0] factor uniquely through H0. The natural automorphism between p-counits induces an automorphism of p*G on H0. Postcompose t with its derived direct image. This preserves its isomorphism property and gives the equation for c. No invertibility of the counit at K is used. The empty cover gives zero throughout.
